function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

### 1. What Turbonomics is and why it matters for a multi‑cloud environment | Feature | Turbonomics (AIOps platform) | Native Cloud AIOps / Observability tools | |---------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------| | **Scope** | Works **across all clouds** (AWS, Azure, GCP, on‑prem, edge) in a single pane of glass | Each provider offers its own siloed solution (e.g., CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, Stackdriver) | | **Data ingestion** | Pulls telemetry from **any source** – cloud APIs, Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, logs, metrics, events, even custom business KPIs | Limited to the provider’s own APIs or integrations | | **AI/ML engine** | Uses **continuous learning** to model performance, capacity, cost, and business value; automatically generates recommendations and auto‑remediation actions | Mostly rule‑based alerts or dashboards; no built‑in predictive or prescriptive AI | | **Cost optimization** | Real‑time cost‑to‑value analysis, right‑sizing, spot/low‑price instance recommendations, and automated scaling | Cost dashboards and budgets, but no AI‑driven right‑sizing or automated scaling | | **Business‑value mapping** | Maps every resource to a **business KPI** (e.g., revenue, customer satisfaction, time‑to‑market) | No direct mapping; you have to build custom dashboards | | **Automation** | Auto‑remediation via APIs, Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes operators, or custom scripts | Manual scaling or scripted automation, but no unified orchestration | | **Governance & compliance** | Policy engine that enforces cost, security, and compliance rules across clouds | Separate policy engines per provider (e.g., AWS Config, Azure Policy) | | **Unified UI & API** | Single console, REST/GraphQL API, SDKs | Multiple consoles and APIs per provider | --- ### 2. How Turbonomics can help Unilever | Business Need | Turbonomics Solution | Expected Impact | |---------------|----------------------|-----------------| | **Unified multi‑cloud observability** | One dashboard that aggregates metrics, logs, events, and cost from AWS, Azure, GCP, and on‑prem | Faster incident response, reduced mean‑time‑to‑repair (MTTR) | | **AI‑driven capacity planning** | Predictive models that forecast CPU, memory, storage, and network usage based on historical trends and upcoming releases | Avoid over‑provisioning, cut idle capacity by 20‑30 % | | **Cost‑to‑value data‑driven budget allocation. 4. **Regulatory compliance** * Policy engine ensures that all data processed in EU regions stays within GDPR‑compliant zones, automatically moving workloads if a
